# Lower Valley irrigation trial

The third quarter closed the field trial of the new irrigation controllers across the twelve partner farms in the Lower Valley. Every site reported through the season, and the controllers ran for 2,184 hours without a missed schedule.

## Summary

Water use fell by 18 percent against the same quarter last year, while yields held within two percent of the average for the last five years. The largest savings came from the three orchards on sandy soil, where the moisture sensors cut evening runs by almost half.

## What we measured

- Water drawn per hectare, read weekly from the farm meters
- Soil moisture at two depths, logged every fifteen minutes
- Yield per block at harvest, reported by each farm manager

## Results by site type

Orchards saw the clearest change. Vineyards on clay held steady, and the two vegetable farms used slightly more water in August during the heat wave, when the controllers correctly extended the morning cycles.

The sensor network itself needed little attention. Two probes were replaced after frost damage in early July, and one gateway lost power for a weekend before its battery was swapped.

## Next steps

1. Extend the trial to the eight farms on the eastern terraces in spring.
2. Share the weekly moisture summaries with farm managers by email.
3. Review the heat wave override with the agronomy team before May.
